incidents.description:
On 6/3/2026, the employee reported experiencing discomfort in his back that he stated began approximately one week prior, on or around 5/27/2026. The employee stated he could not recall a specific event or location associated with the discomfort. The employee reported that his pain level had decreased from a 7 to a 4 since 05/27/2026.

On 6/4/2026, the employee was taken to Trinity Family Medicine for evaluation. The employee was evaluated and released to full duty without restrictions.

On 6-4-26 at approximately [12:22am], the employee was operating Unit 63141 and was exiting the location when the unit crossed a steel plate cover. As the unit crossed the plate, both saddle fuel tanks contacted the plate and bottomed out, and both tanks began to leak diesel fuel. The unit was immediately moved into secondary containment. No injuries were reported.

The employee stated that he was traveling northbound on FM 179 and negotiating a right-hand curve onto CR 6000, just outside of Shallowater, Texas, during heavy rainfall. While navigating the curve, the rear tires lost traction. The employee released the accelerator in an attempt to regain control of the vehicle. When traction was regained, the truck rotated and became perpendicular to the roadway, exited the road, and rolled an estimated three times.

No other vehicles were involved in the incident.

Following the rollover, the employee called 911 and notified management of the accident. Sheriff's deputies and emergency medical personnel responded to the scene. The employee was evaluated by paramedics and released at the scene without transport.

The employee was subsequently taken to Occupational Medicine (OccMed) for further evaluation and was released to full duty with no restrictions.

No crash report number was provided to the driver, and no citations were issued.

Management arranged for the vehicle to be transported back to the BTI yard in Midland.
